nodes.title: How will this wallet be structured?
nodes.body:
**Educational presentation — not financial advice.**

Who holds the keys that authorize spending?

choices.label: Use a custodian
choices.description: A company or service holds the keys that spend your bitcoin. You trade convenience for counterparty risk.

choices.label: Self-custodied
choices.description: You (or a group you choose) hold the keys. You are responsible for backups, devices, and recovery.

nodes.title: Which custody model?
nodes.body: A third party holds Bitcoin on your behalf. You hold an account claim — not necessarily on-chain keys.

choices.label: Single custodian
choices.description: One exchange or hosted wallet holds the keys. Simple, but you trust that venue.

choices.label: Federated custody
choices.description: A group or federation shares custody under threshold rules.

nodes.title: Which custodian?
nodes.body: Pick a recognizable service. Icons are brand marks; offerings change — verify current features yourself.

choices.label: Kraken
choices.subtitle: Exchange · Lightning · Lending-related
choices.description: Use Kraken as the single custodian for this educational path.

choices.label: Coinbase
choices.subtitle: Exchange
choices.description: Use Coinbase as the single custodian for this educational path.

choices.label: Stacks
choices.subtitle: Stacks ecosystem · stacks.co
choices.description: Use a Stacks-related custodial or hosted path.

choices.label: Coinos
choices.subtitle: Web wallet · Lightning · Custodial options
choices.description: Use Coinos as a lightweight hosted option.

choices.label: Bull Bitcoin
choices.subtitle: Exchange · Buy / sell
choices.description: Bull Bitcoin. Exchange · Buy / sell. Choose this if it matches how you will actually operate.

choices.label: Wallet of Satoshi
choices.subtitle: Lightning · Custodial (supported regions)
choices.description: Use Wallet of Satoshi (custodial Lightning convenience).

choices.label: Bitcoin Well
choices.subtitle: Buy / sell · Related services
choices.description: Bitcoin Well. Buy / sell · Related services. Choose this if it matches how you will actually operate.

nodes.title: How will you secure the Kraken account?
nodes.body: Baseline: **username + password**. Typically: TOTP, passkeys, hardware security keys; Global Settings Lock. SMS is weaker (SIM-swap).

choices.label: Password only (no 2FA)
choices.description: No extra authentication beyond password. Weak against phishing and credential stuffing.

choices.label: SMS 2FA
choices.description: SMS one-time codes. Better than nothing, but vulnerable to SIM-swap attacks.

choices.label: Authenticator (TOTP)
choices.description: Authenticator-app codes. Stronger than SMS; still phishable on fake login pages.

choices.label: Passkey
choices.description: Passkeys / WebAuthn resist many phishing sites when the browser and site support them.

choices.label: Hardware security key
choices.description: Hardware security keys (FIDO2/U2F) for phishing-resistant second factor.

choices.label: Email recovery reliance
choices.description: Email-based codes or magic links. Convenient; email account takeover becomes critical.

nodes.title: How will you secure the Coinbase account?
nodes.body: Baseline: **username + password**. Typically TOTP / SMS / passkey-style MFA. SMS remains SIM-swap exposed.

choices.label: Password only (no 2FA)
choices.description: Password only on Coinbase. High risk if the password leaks or is phished.

choices.label: SMS 2FA
choices.description: SMS 2FA on Coinbase — watch for SIM-swap.

choices.label: Authenticator (TOTP)
choices.description: Authenticator 2FA on Coinbase.

choices.label: Passkey / platform MFA
choices.description: Passkey login where Coinbase offers it.

choices.label: Hardware security key
choices.description: Hardware security key as 2FA on Coinbase.

nodes.body: Auth varies by product. Treat like a common web custodian unless you verify otherwise.

choices.label: Password only (no 2FA)
choices.description: Password only on Stacks wallet/service path.

choices.label: SMS 2FA
choices.description: SMS 2FA — SIM-swap risk remains.

choices.label: Authenticator (TOTP)
choices.description: Authenticator-app 2FA.

choices.label: Passkey (if offered)
choices.description: Passkey-based authentication where available.

choices.label: Hardware security key (if offered)
choices.description: Hardware security key 2FA.

choices.description: Authenticator codes for Coinos.

nodes.title: What remains on this custodial path?
nodes.body:
**Operable account claim** — auth hardening helps takeover risk; it does **not** remove counterparty risk (insolvency, freeze, seizure, KYC).

Apply paired mitigations above. Continue hardening below — or leave only if comparing structures.

choices.label: Revisit another custodian's auth
choices.description: Stay on this custodial path and strengthen login / withdrawal controls.

choices.label: Compare self-custody instead
choices.description: Leave custody and move toward keys you control.

choices.label: Compare federated custody
choices.description: Explore a federated / community custody model instead.

choices.label: Explore another structure…
choices.subtitle: Optional — leave this path
choices.description: Optional detour: start over with a different custody structure.

nodes.title: Which federation style?
nodes.body: Operators jointly custody or mint claims. Trust: federation membership, threshold, and **your** seed/claim backup.

choices.label: Fedi
choices.subtitle: Federation · Community custody
choices.description: Community federation custody via Fedi-style setups.

choices.label: Lightning community / federation
choices.subtitle: Payments · Privacy (e-cash where relevant)
choices.description: Lightning community / federation. Payments · Privacy (e-cash where relevant). Choose this if it matches how you will actually operate.

nodes.title: How will you back up your Fedi claim?
nodes.body: Community / federation custody. Vulns: guardian collusion, phishing of federation seeds, jurisdictional seizure, hard recovery if keys are lost.

choices.label: Document seed/claim backup + guardians
choices.description: Document how federation recovery and guardian claims work before you deposit.

choices.label: Rely on app recovery only
choices.description: Skip careful backup documentation — high loss risk if guardians or seeds are unclear.

nodes.title: How will you secure federated Lightning access?
nodes.body: Same core risks: **collusion**, phishing, concentrated jurisdiction, and seed/claim loss.

choices.label: Offline claim backup + threshold notes
choices.description: Document Lightning federation recovery and channel/claim procedures.

choices.label: Device-only, no offline backup
choices.description: Proceed without solid recovery documentation.

nodes.title: What remains on this federated path?
nodes.body: **Profile:** community trust instead of a single company; often better privacy UX. Residual: collusion, legal concentration, seed loss without exchange-style recovery.

choices.label: Strengthen backup playbook
choices.description: Improve federation backup and guardian documentation.

choices.label: Compare single-key self-custody
choices.description: Move from federation custody toward self-custody.

choices.label: Explore another structure…
choices.subtitle: Optional — leave this path
choices.description: Optional detour: start over with a different custody structure.

nodes.title: Single key or multisignature?
nodes.body: You hold the keys. Structure matters: one key vs multisignature.

choices.label: Single key
choices.description: One key (or one seed) can spend. Simpler than multisig, but a single failure can lose funds.

choices.label: Multisignature
choices.description: Several keys must cooperate to spend (m-of-n). Removes some single points of failure; adds operational complexity.

nodes.title: Which single-key tool?
nodes.body: Choose the device or software that will hold or sign with the key. Tool choice unlocks different seed, storage, and protection options.

choices.label: Ledger
choices.subtitle: Hardware · USB / Bluetooth
choices.description: Ledger hardware wallets keep keys in a secure element and sign on-device. Next you will pick the exact model.

choices.label: Trezor
choices.subtitle: Hardware · USB
choices.description: Trezor hardware wallets emphasize open design and on-device confirmation. Next you will pick the exact model.

choices.label: Coldcard
choices.subtitle: Hardware · air-gap oriented · SD
choices.description: Coldcard is a Bitcoin-focused, air-gap oriented hardware signer. Next you will pick Mk4, Mk5, or Q.

choices.label: Bitkey
choices.subtitle: Mobile + hardware (2-of-3 style)
choices.description: Bitkey combines a hardware device with a phone app in a seedless 2-of-3 recovery design. Next you confirm the product.

choices.label: Seedsigner
choices.subtitle: Air-gapped · DIY · QR only
choices.description: DIY air-gapped signer that does not store the seed after power-off. Next you confirm the kit style.

choices.label: Jade
choices.subtitle: Blockstream · optional blind oracle
choices.description: Blockstream Jade hardware wallet with optional blind-oracle features. Next you pick Classic, Core, or Plus.

choices.label: Tails OS
choices.subtitle: Live amnesic OS · desktop
choices.description: Boot an amnesic live OS and run wallet software there. Strong OPSEC if you never break the air-gap casually.

choices.label: Smartphone
choices.subtitle: Hot · internet-connected
choices.description: A normal internet-connected phone wallet. Convenient for spending; high malware and phishing exposure.

choices.label: Air-gapped smartphone
choices.subtitle: Offline phone signer
choices.description: A phone kept offline as a signer. Installation and updates must not silently reintroduce network risk.

choices.label: BlueWallet
choices.subtitle: Mobile app · hot / watch-only
choices.description: Popular mobile Bitcoin wallet. Can be hot (holds seed) or watch-only (xpub only).

choices.label: Bitcoin Core / Bitcoin-Qt
choices.subtitle: Full node · desktop wallet
choices.description: Full node wallet on a computer. Powerful and sovereign; the machine is usually a hot surface if online.

choices.label: Manual seed + signing device
choices.subtitle: Dice / DIY entropy → load signer
choices.description: Create entropy yourself (dice, cards, etc.) then load a signer. Maximum control; easy to get wrong without discipline.

nodes.title: Which Ledger product?
nodes.body: Ledger makes several hardware wallets. Pick the model you will actually use — features and recovery UX differ by device.

choices.label: Nano S Plus
choices.description: Compact USB device with a clearer screen than the original Nano S. A common choice for computer-connected cold storage.
choices.subtitle: USB · Secure Element

choices.label: Nano X
choices.description: Portable Ledger with Bluetooth for mobile companion apps, plus USB. Convenient, but treat wireless pairing as part of the threat model.
choices.subtitle: USB / Bluetooth · Secure Element

choices.label: Nano Gen5
choices.description: Current-generation Nano form factor. Confirm the exact model and firmware on Ledger’s site before you buy or restore.
choices.subtitle: USB · next-gen Nano

choices.label: Flex
choices.description: Larger touchscreen Ledger for clearer address review. Still verify every receive address and firmware authenticity.
choices.subtitle: Touchscreen · Secure Element

choices.label: Stax
choices.description: Premium E Ink touchscreen device aimed at clearer transaction review. Same seed and supply-chain discipline as other Ledgers.
choices.subtitle: E Ink touchscreen · Secure Element

choices.label: Nano S (legacy)
choices.description: Older USB-only model. Fine if you already own one and keep firmware current, but new buyers usually prefer Nano S Plus or newer.
choices.subtitle: Discontinued · USB only

nodes.body: Trezor’s current Safe line differs from older Model One / Model T devices. Choose the unit you will set up and verify.

choices.label: Safe 3
choices.description: Entry Safe-series device with a secure element. Straightforward USB setup for single-sig cold storage.
choices.subtitle: USB · Secure Element

choices.label: Safe 5
choices.description: Touchscreen Safe-series wallet for easier on-device confirmation. Still buy from a trusted channel and verify firmware.
choices.subtitle: USB · touchscreen

choices.label: Safe 7
choices.description: Current flagship Safe-series model. Use official docs for the exact feature set and recovery flow on your firmware.
choices.subtitle: USB · flagship Safe

choices.label: Model One (legacy)
choices.description: Older button-based Trezor. Still usable if you already own it; new purchases should prefer the Safe line.
choices.subtitle: Discontinued

choices.label: Model T (legacy / discontinued)
choices.description: Previous touchscreen flagship, now discontinued for new retail in many channels. Prefer Safe 5 / Safe 7 for new setups.
choices.subtitle: Discontinued · touchscreen

nodes.title: Which Coldcard product?
nodes.body: Coldcard devices are air-gap oriented and Bitcoin-focused. Mk4, Mk5, and Q differ mainly in keyboard, display, and workflow comfort.

choices.label: Mk4
choices.description: Established Coldcard with numeric keypad and strong air-gap workflows (PSBT via SD). Widely documented for multisig and dice entropy.
choices.subtitle: Air-gap · SD / USB

choices.label: Mk5
choices.description: Newer Mk-series Coldcard when available in your channel. Confirm current Coinkite naming and firmware before purchase.
choices.subtitle: Air-gap · next Mk

choices.label: Coldcard Q
choices.description: Coldcard with a full keyboard and QR-friendly flows. Useful if you want faster air-gap text entry without a host keyboard.
choices.subtitle: Full keyboard · QR

nodes.title: Which Bitkey product?
nodes.body: Bitkey is a mobile-first self-custody design. Understand the 2-of-3 recovery model before you fund it.

choices.label: Bitkey device
choices.description: Block’s Bitkey pairs a hardware key with your phone app. Spending uses a 2-of-3 arrangement across the device, the phone, and a Block recovery server — there is no traditional BIP39 seed phrase to write down. Take the recovery and server-dependence model seriously before large balances.
choices.subtitle: Hardware + phone · seedless 2-of-3

nodes.title: Which Seedsigner product?
nodes.body: Seedsigner is a DIY, stateless air-gapped signer. The kit does not keep your seed after power-off.

choices.label: DIY Seedsigner kit
choices.description: Build or buy a Raspberry Pi Zero–based Seedsigner. It is stateless: seeds live on your backup (metal/paper), not on the device after shutdown. Ideal for air-gapped QR signing when you accept DIY responsibility.
choices.subtitle: Raspberry Pi Zero · stateless · QR

nodes.title: How will you generate the Ledger seed?
nodes.body: Ledger creates BIP39 on-device. Prefer adding user entropy when available. Seed stays on device; optional passphrase.

choices.label: Device RNG only
choices.description: Let the Ledger create the seed with its built-in random number generator only.

choices.label: Device RNG + user entropy
choices.description: Combine device RNG with extra entropy you provide, following Ledger’s documented flow carefully.

nodes.title: PIN and passphrase on Ledger?
nodes.body: PIN protects the device. BIP39 passphrase creates a hidden wallet — backup separately and test recovery.

choices.label: PIN + passphrase (tested)
choices.description: Set a device PIN and a BIP39 passphrase you have tested in recovery. Passphrase is a second secret.

choices.label: PIN only
choices.description: Protect the device with a strong PIN only (no BIP39 passphrase).

choices.label: Skip extra protection
choices.description: Skip PIN/passphrase hardening for now — high physical and theft risk.

nodes.title: How will you generate the Trezor seed?
nodes.body: Trezor generates BIP39 on-device. Shamir (SLIP39) is an advanced option on some models — educational path sticks to BIP39.

choices.label: Device RNG only
choices.description: Let the Trezor create the seed using device RNG only.

choices.label: Add computer/keyboard entropy
choices.description: Add entropy from the companion computer/keyboard as documented by Trezor.

nodes.title: PIN and passphrase on Trezor?
nodes.body: PIN on-device; optional passphrase. Verify firmware signatures on first use.

choices.label: PIN + passphrase (tested)
choices.description: PIN plus tested BIP39 passphrase on Trezor.

choices.label: PIN only
choices.description: Strong PIN only on Trezor.

choices.label: Skip extra protection
choices.description: Skip extra device protection for now.

nodes.title: How will you generate the Coldcard seed?
nodes.body: Coldcard favors dice rolls and air-gapped ops (SD/QR). Seed can live on device or be wiped after backup.

choices.label: Dice rolls on device
choices.description: Enter dice rolls on the Coldcard so seed entropy includes physical randomness you control.

choices.label: Device RNG
choices.description: Use the Coldcard’s own RNG to create the seed.

nodes.title: Where will the Coldcard seed live?
nodes.body: Seed on device (PIN/passphrase), or ephemeral: backup to metal/SD then wipe for ultra-airgap posture.

choices.label: Seed on device + PIN / passphrase
choices.description: Keep the seed on the Coldcard behind PIN/passphrase and treat the device as long-lived.

choices.label: Encrypted backup on SD + PIN
choices.description: Use encrypted SD backup workflows with PIN discipline.

choices.label: Metal backup then wipe device
choices.description: Back up to metal (or equivalent), then wipe the device so it holds no seed at rest.

nodes.title: How will Bitkey hold key material?
nodes.body: Bitkey uses a mobile + hardware collaborative design (typically 2-of-3). Cloud assist eases recovery — and reintroduces dependency.

choices.label: Standard setup (mobile + hardware + recovery)
choices.description: Use Bitkey’s normal mobile + hardware + recovery-server setup. Understand who can help recover.

choices.label: Minimize cloud recovery reliance
choices.description: Configure to reduce reliance on cloud/server recovery where the product allows — know what you give up.

nodes.title: Device PIN / app lock?
nodes.body: Protect the hardware and phone with strong PIN/biometrics; understand recovery paths before funding.

choices.label: Strong PIN + app lock
choices.description: Strong device PIN and phone app lock before funding.

choices.label: Weak / default protection
choices.description: Weak or default locks — avoid for meaningful balances.

nodes.title: How will Seedsigner create entropy?
nodes.body: Seedsigner is typically **stateless**: generate, backup, sign via QR — seed not stored on device between sessions.

choices.label: Dice entropy
choices.description: Create entropy with dice on Seedsigner, then back up the resulting seed offline.

choices.label: Camera / image entropy
choices.description: Use camera/image entropy on Seedsigner. Keep cameras and shoulders away from sensitive screens.

nodes.title: How will you store the Seedsigner backup?
nodes.body: No persistent seed on device means **your metal/paper backup is the wallet**. Geographic diversity matters.

choices.label: Metal backup (verified restore)
choices.description: Stamp or engrave the seed on metal and verify a restore. For Seedsigner, the backup is the wallet.

choices.label: Paper only
choices.description: Paper backup only — vulnerable to fire, water, and wear.

choices.label: No durable backup yet
choices.description: No durable backup yet — catastrophic if the seed is lost.

choices.label: Device RNG
choices.description: Let Jade create the seed with device RNG.

choices.label: RNG + blind oracle assist
choices.description: Use Jade RNG with optional blind-oracle assist as documented by Blockstream.

choices.description: PIN plus tested passphrase on Jade.

choices.label: PIN only
choices.description: PIN only on Jade.

choices.label: Skip extra protection
choices.description: Skip extra protection for now.

nodes.title: Which wallet tooling on Tails?
nodes.body: Tails is an amnesic live OS. **Electrum does not generate BIP39** — stay Electrum-native or use BIP39-capable offline tooling.

choices.label: Electrum (non-BIP39)
choices.description: Electrum on Tails. Note: Electrum seeds are not BIP39 — plan recovery tooling carefully.

choices.label: BIP39-capable offline tooling
choices.description: BIP39-capable offline tools on Tails with verified software only.

nodes.title: How will you keep Tails air-gapped?
nodes.body: Never "just enable Wi‑Fi" to install packages. Ferry verified software via USB.

choices.label: USB ferry + verified builds only
choices.description: Move software only via verified USB ferry; never casually enable networking.

choices.label: Occasionally connect for updates
choices.description: Occasionally connect Tails for updates — weakens the air-gap story.

nodes.title: Hot phone or move toward air-gap?
nodes.body: A normal smartphone wallet is **hot**. Malware, fake apps, and seed phishing dominate risk.

choices.label: Keep as hot spending wallet
choices.description: Accept a hot phone wallet for spending convenience.

choices.label: Dedicate as air-gapped phone instead
choices.description: Repurpose the phone as an offline signer instead.

nodes.title: How will the phone create the seed?
nodes.body: App RNG is convenient. Avoid cloud screenshots and support that asks for seed words.

choices.label: App-generated BIP39
choices.description: Let the app generate a BIP39 seed on the phone.

nodes.title: How will you back up the phone wallet?
nodes.body: Cloud backups of seeds are high risk. Prefer offline metal/paper; never screenshots.

choices.label: Offline metal / paper (no cloud)
choices.description: Offline metal or paper backup; no cloud photos of the seed.

choices.label: Cloud / screenshot backup
choices.description: Cloud or screenshot backup — high leak risk.

choices.label: No backup yet
choices.description: No backup yet.

nodes.title: How will you install signing software offline?
nodes.body: Air-gap fails when people break it to install apps. Use USB ferry of verified APKs; disable radios.

choices.label: USB ferry + verified builds
choices.description: Install signing apps via USB ferry and verify builds offline.

choices.label: Briefly go online to install
choices.description: Briefly go online to install — reintroduces malware risk.

nodes.title: How will the air-gapped phone create the seed?
nodes.body: Generate BIP39 offline; write the seed; confirm restore produces the same first address.

choices.label: Generate BIP39 on phone
choices.description: Generate BIP39 on the offline phone and write the seed securely.

nodes.title: Hot wallet or watch-only in BlueWallet?
nodes.body: BlueWallet can hold keys (hot) or import an xpub as watch-only. Lightning features may be custodial — check current mode.

choices.label: Hot: create seed
choices.description: BlueWallet holds a seed and can spend — treat the phone as hot.

choices.label: Watch-only (xpub from cold device)
choices.description: Import an xpub only; spending stays on a cold device.

nodes.title: How will BlueWallet get the seed?
nodes.body: App RNG generates BIP39. Keep backups offline.

choices.label: App-generated BIP39
choices.description: App-generated BIP39 seed in BlueWallet.

nodes.title: Descriptors or legacy wallet.dat?
nodes.body: Bitcoin Core on an online PC is a **hot** wallet unless the machine is dedicated/air-gapped. Prefer descriptor wallets.

choices.label: Create descriptor wallet
choices.description: Create a modern descriptor wallet in Bitcoin Core.

choices.label: Import descriptors / keys
choices.description: Import descriptors or keys into Core.

choices.label: Watch-only descriptors
choices.description: Watch-only descriptors — public side only until you add signing keys elsewhere.

nodes.title: Is this PC treated as hot or dedicated?
nodes.body: Online full node + wallet = hot malware surface. Dedicated offline machine changes the threat model.

choices.label: Online PC (hot)
choices.description: This PC stays online with the wallet — hot malware surface.

choices.label: Dedicated / offline machine
choices.description: Use a dedicated or offline machine to reduce malware exposure.

nodes.title: How will you create physical entropy?
nodes.body: You generate entropy yourself, then derive a BIP39 seed (often via a hardware device that mixes or maps your entropy). Apply ceremony OPSEC below before choosing a method.

choices.label: Dice rolling
choices.description: Roll physical dice to build entropy for a BIP39 seed.

choices.label: Entropy + hardware device
choices.subtitle: You supply entropy · device hashes to seed
choices.description: You supply entropy; a hardware device mixes it into a seed.

choices.label: Coin flips
choices.description: Coin flips mapped to bits/words — easy to bias if process is sloppy.

choices.label: Playing cards
choices.description: Playing-card entropy with a documented mapping.

nodes.title: Which device will mix your entropy?
nodes.body: You provide entropy; the device hashes/mixes it with its RNG to produce the seed. Prefer devices with clear user-entropy procedures.

choices.label: Coldcard
choices.subtitle: Dice / user entropy on device
choices.description: Coldcard will mix your user entropy on-device.

choices.label: Seedsigner
choices.subtitle: Dice or camera entropy
choices.description: Seedsigner will mix dice or camera entropy.

choices.label: Blockstream Jade
choices.subtitle: RNG + optional oracle / user entropy
choices.description: Jade will mix entropy (optional oracle assist).

choices.label: Ledger
choices.subtitle: Device RNG + user entropy
choices.description: Ledger will combine device RNG with your entropy.

choices.label: Trezor
choices.subtitle: Computer / keyboard entropy
choices.description: Trezor will accept computer/keyboard entropy.

choices.label: Other entropy methods
choices.description: Return to other manual entropy methods.

nodes.title: Which device will take dice rolls?
nodes.body: These devices can generate a BIP39 seed from dice rolls you provide on-device.

choices.label: Coldcard
choices.subtitle: Dice rolls on device
choices.description: Coldcard. Dice rolls on device. Choose this if it matches how you will actually operate.

choices.label: Seedsigner

nodes.title: How will dice become a seed?
nodes.body: Map rolls yourself with a trusted table, or use a hardware device that accepts dice rolls and derives the BIP39 seed.

nodes.title: How will multisig keys be distributed?
nodes.body: **m-of-n** keys to spend. Independence is the point: same-vendor or same-country stacks correlate risk.

choices.label: Home · family · bank (same country)
choices.subtitle: Geographic / jurisdiction concentration
choices.description: Keys stay in one country — correlated legal and physical risk.

choices.label: Multi-vendor devices
choices.subtitle: Same-vendor multisig ≠ independent
choices.description: Multi-vendor devices. Same-vendor multisig ≠ independent. Choose this if it matches how you will actually operate.

choices.label: Different cities / countries
choices.description: Spread keys across different cities or countries.

choices.label: Collaborative custody provider
choices.description: Collaborative custody provider. This option continues the path and may add specific risks shown under the button.

choices.label: All keys one vendor (anti-pattern)
choices.description: All keys on the same vendor hardware — correlated firmware/supply risk.

nodes.title: Accept same-country risk or diversify?
nodes.body: Same-country stacks share **legal jurisdiction**, local disaster correlation, and easier coercion. Prefer geographic diversity when stakes warrant it.

choices.label: Spread across cities / countries
choices.description: Spread across cities / countries. This option continues the path and may add specific risks shown under the button.

choices.label: Also diversify device vendors
choices.description: Also diversify device vendors. This option continues the path and may add specific risks shown under the button.

nodes.title: Switch away from same-vendor multisig?
nodes.body: If all signers share firmware, RNG, and supply chain, **one vendor bug can hit your threshold**. Prefer multi-vendor.

choices.label: Switch to multi-vendor
choices.description: Switch to multi-vendor. This option continues the path and may add specific risks shown under the button.

choices.label: Continue anyway (not recommended)
choices.description: Continue anyway (not recommended). This option continues the path and may add specific risks shown under the button.

nodes.body: Distinct manufacturers, purchase channels, and entropy sources. Export and backup the **wallet descriptor**.

choices.description: Yes — distribute locations / parties. This option continues the path and may add specific risks shown under the button.

choices.label: Open multisig path summary

nodes.title: Add independent human parties?
nodes.body: Keys in **different locations**. Still ensure you can assemble *m* keys when you need to spend or rotate.

choices.label: Open multisig path summary
choices.description: Move toward an m-of-n multisignature structure.

nodes.title: Peer humans or a collaborative-custody firm?
nodes.body: Co-signers: spouse, attorney, firm, friend. Pros: inheritance & travel. Cons: collusion; a co-sign **service** can become custodian-like.

choices.label: Collaborative-custody key agent
choices.description: Include a key-agent / cosigner firm (more convenience, more trust).

choices.label: Only peer humans (no firm)
choices.description: Only peer humans — no corporate key agent.

choices.label: Open multisig path summary
choices.description: Move toward an m-of-n multisignature structure.

nodes.title: Can you still spend if the firm disappears?
nodes.body: Keep *m* such that you can still spend if the firm vanishes (e.g. 2-of-3 where you hold 2).

choices.label: Yes — I retain spending threshold
choices.description: Yes — I retain spending threshold. This option continues the path and may add specific risks shown under the button.

choices.label: No — firm is required to spend
choices.description: Skip stronger authentication for now. Only appropriate for tiny balances you can afford to lose.

nodes.title: Will you practice a recovery drill?
nodes.body: Document legal/practical expectations; practice recovery with a **test** wallet first.

choices.description: Schedule a recovery drill so the quorum actually works under stress.

choices.label: Skip drill for now
choices.description: Skip drills for now — discover broken recovery when it is too late.

choices.description: Seeds + descriptor + playbook. This option continues the path and may add specific risks shown under the button.

choices.label: Seeds only (no descriptor)
choices.description: Seeds only (no descriptor). This option continues the path and may add specific risks shown under the button.
